s01.translation: Our Father, who art in heaven,

s04.translation: Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

s05.translation: Give us this day our daily bread.

s06.translation: And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

s07.translation: And lead us not into temptation,

s08.translation: but deliver us from evil. Amen.

w001.function: Vocative — direct address to God; the whole prayer is speech to a Thou.

w002.function: Possessive in the vocative, agreeing with “Pater”: not “my” but “our” — the prayer of a community.

w003.function: Relative pronoun in the nominative — opens the relative clause about the addressee.

w005.function: Preposition with the ablative — place: where?

w006.function: Ablative plural — literally “in the heavens”: the plural follows the Hebrew idiom; the received English renders it singular. A curiosity: singular “caelum” is neuter, but the plural (“caeli”) is masculine.

w007.function: Present subjunctive, passive — a wish-petition: “may it be made holy”. First of three petitions in this mood.

w008.function: Nominative — the subject: what is to be hallowed?

w010.function: Optative subjunctive — the second petition: “may it come”.

w011.function: Nominative — the subject: what is to come?

w013.function: Subjunctive of “fio” (to become) — the third petition. The same “fiat” Mary answers with at the Annunciation (Lk 1:38).

w014.function: Nominative — the subject: what is to be done?

w020.function: Preposition with the ablative — place: “on earth”.

w024.function: “quotidiánus” — daily; the Latin rendering of the Greek “epioúsios”, a word almost unattested outside this prayer.

w025.function: Imperative, 2nd person — the first petition voiced as a direct imperative (the negative petition will use the subjunctive instead).

w031.function: Literally “debts” (debitum — what is owed); the received English says “trespasses”.

w033.function: Comparative conjunction — opens the comparison with our own forgiving.

w035.function: Nominative — the subject spelled out for emphasis.

w036.function: 1st person plural, indicative — a statement of fact, not a petition: this is what we do.

w037.function: Dative plural — literally “to the debtors”: whom we forgive.

w040.function: “ne” with the subjunctive — a negative petition: “that Thou not…”.

w042.function: Subjunctive after “ne” — literally “bring into”; the received English keeps “lead”.

w043.function: “in” with the ACCUSATIVE — direction: “into temptation”. Compare “in” (w005), where the ablative marks place.

w044.function: Accusative, 3rd declension — the goal of motion after “in”.

w045.function: Adversative conjunction — the petition turns: not into temptation, but toward deliverance.

w048.function: Preposition “a” with the ablative: from what / from whom.

w049.function: Ablative after “a”. The form leaves the gender open: neuter “malum” (evil) or masculine “malus” (the Evil One)? The tradition reads both senses at once.

w050.function: Hebrew “so be it” — indeclinable, taken over by Latin as it stands.
